notes: Derived edit. Planet types are individuals (instance_of). The definitional premise 'a moon orbits a planet of a given type exactly when the planet it orbits is of that type' is a SWRL rule one way (orbits_planet_of_type is functional, so it can't be a chain target) and a class axiom per type the other way, so the premise route reaches an unnamed planet. The two types exclude each other (one_type: the bridge 'a planet cannot be both', stated in q0 and q3 since 2026-10-31). q1's original 'no' needs a gas giant to lack a solid surface: the q1 bridge 'Gas giants have no solid surface' since 2026-10-31 (surface).

type_rule: orbits_planet_of_type value gas_giant ⊑ orbits some (instance_of value gas_giant)
orbits_planet_of_type value terrestrial ⊑ orbits some (instance_of value terrestrial)
